b1-kerak-emas.title: No Obligation: kerak emas
b1-kerak-emas.explanation: To say something ISN'T necessary (rather than forbidden), Uzbek negates kerak itself with emas: sizga bugun kelishingiz kerak emas (you don't need to come today) -- the infinitive stays exactly as it is in the positive obligation sentence, only kerak gets negated.
b1-kerak-emas.fact: This is a genuinely different meaning from bormang ("don't go", a real prohibition) -- kerak emas says the action is simply optional, not banned, a distinction English also makes ("don't have to" vs. "must not") but that's easy to blur when translating word-for-word.

dialogue.en: Do I need to come tomorrow?
No, you don't need to come.

items.en: You don't need to come today.

items.uz: Menga bu kitobni o'qishim kerak emas.
items.en: I don't need to read this book.
We don't need to leave now.

items.uz: Senga bu ishni tugatishing kerak emas.
items.en: You don't need to finish this task.

items.uz: Ularga bu haqda bilishlari kerak emas.
items.en: They don't need to know about this.

items.uz: Menga har kuni borishim kerak emas.
items.en: I don't need to go every day.

items.uz: Bizga ko'p pul sarflashimiz kerak emas.
items.en: We don't need to spend a lot of money.
He/she doesn't need to work today.
